data.name: Aydarus
data.gender_notes: Aydarus is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root ‘Awdara’, meaning to help, support or assist. In Islamic history, Aydarus is mentioned as a title of certain saints and scholars who provided aid and support to the Islamic community. The name Aydarus carries the meaning “Helper, Supporter” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aydarus usually hope their child will grow to embody helper, supporter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes the essence of a righteous helper, aiding and supporting others in their spiritual and worldly journeys.
data.etymology: Aydarus belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Helper, Supporter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aydarus total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

This is evident in the many historical figures who held the title, including various scholars and saints who selflessly dedicated their lives to the betterment of their communities. The concept of giving aid and support is deeply ingrained in Islamic teachings, and the name Aydarus serves as a reminder of this principle in daily life.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the name Aydarus represents the idea of serving as a source of help and support for others, particularly in times of need. This selfless act of providing aid is considered a virtue in Islam, and those who embody this trait are held in high esteem. The name Aydarus serves as a reminder for believers to look for opportunities to help their fellow human beings, and to strive towards being a source of support and comfort in transient and chaotic times.

historical_references.reference: Aydarus is mentioned in the historical records as the name of an Umayyad governor of Ifriqiya (present-day Tunisia) during the reign of Caliph Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik (724-743 AD). He is known for his military campaigns against the Berber tribes and his attempts to expand the Umayyad Empire in North Africa.
historical_references.context: Umayyad Empire, Ifriqiya, Military campaigns, Berber tribes

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Aydarus can be found in the works of Ibn Abd al-Hakam, a 9th century historian. He mentions Aydarus as the name of a governor of Kufa (present-day Iraq) during the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 AD). Aydarus is known for his role in suppressing a rebellion led by the Mukhannathun, a group of effeminate men who had seized power in Kufa and were causing instability in the region.
historical_references.context: Abbasid Caliphate, Kufa, Suppression of rebellion, Mukhannathun
